page: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 16 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, 16 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with 360 GB of NVMe SSD space. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the cpx51 delivers average performance across most multi-core and memory operations. While its single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is categorized in the bottom 10%, its multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also register average performance. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as Passmark encryption and bzip3 decompression, consistently achieve average tier results.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, as reflected in the lower single-core benchmark results, but it provides a cost-efficient resource density for multi-threaded workloads. With 360 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and average database operation benchmarks, this server is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores.
